summary: On the appearance and disappearance days of his spiritual master, Indradyumna Swami offers a heartfelt personal glorification of Srila Prabhupada, calling him the be-all and end-all of his existence and the one through whom he understands Krishna consciousness. He recalls how Prabhupada himself always deflected praise, saying 'I do not know who is Krishna, I only know my Guru Maharaja,' attributing everything to his own guru, Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakura. The Swami then narrates his own journey: as a teenager he sold all his possessions in a yard sale for about $1,850, joined the Detroit temple, was shaved up within fifteen minutes, and gave his first Srimad Bhagavatam class within seventy-two hours. He shares intimate memories, including missing initiation by a few days and offering Prabhupada his last $10 with a note, then receiving a personal letter promising to accept him as an initiated disciple, with a postscript that he too misses his own Guru Maharaja but always feels him watching over and protecting him. The bulk of the lecture recounts accompanying Prabhupada on a flight from New York to London, where he nervously prepared oranges as prasadam, ate the burning orange peels as maha-prasada (keeping the last one for six months like Madhavendra Puri's sweet rice), and witnessed Prabhupada laughing at a Charlie Chaplin film and teaching that Krishna is the source of all original things and that we must learn to see Krishna everywhere. He describes being made to wait for a lost suitcase full of Prabhupada's Sanskrit and Bengali reference books, missing the kirtan and feast, then improperly dragging it into Prabhupada's room and receiving a hard slap on the back along with the benediction: 'so much endeavor in this material world; when I take you back home to Godhead, everything will be easy and sublime.' He closes with the Paris story of a three-month Metro book-distribution marathon undertaken to win the honor of washing Prabhupada's feet, after which he and his godbrother secretly drank the entire bowl of charanamrita (foot-wash water) while brahmacharis pounded on the locked office door, using these memories to encourage devotees to keep serving despite opposition and difficulty in preaching.
key_points: The spiritual master, whether diksha or shiksha guru, is as dear as one's very life; Prabhupada himself modeled this by always crediting his guru Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakura, who once lectured on the first verse of Srimad Bhagavatam for three months in Dhaka.

The Swami's rapid conversion story: at about age eighteen he sold everything he owned (approximately $1,850) in a yard sale, was shaved up within fifteen minutes of joining, and gave his first Bhagavatam class within seventy-two hours.

Having narrowly missed initiation, he gave Prabhupada his last $10 with a note and later received a personal letter promising future initiation, with a postscript that Prabhupada also feels separation from his own guru yet feels him always watching over and protecting him.

Cited the Chaitanya-caritamrita pastime of Mukunda Datta, whom Lord Chaitanya said He would accept only after a million births, at which the devotee danced in ecstasy because at least acceptance was guaranteed; in Krishna consciousness, separation from the guru deepens attachment rather than healing it.

The airplane orange/prasadam story: he nervously served Prabhupada oranges, ate the stinging orange peels as maha-prasada, and preserved the last peel for six months, comparing it to Madhavendra Puri treasuring the sweet rice stolen by Kshira-chora Gopinatha (Gopinatha stealing the condensed milk).

Prabhupada's teaching from the Charlie Chaplin film on the flight: 'Krishna is the source of all original things,' Chaplin's humor is original so he was seeing Krishna in it, and 'we have to learn to see Krishna everywhere.'

Two central benedictions/teachings frame the endeavor of devotional service: after the hard slap in London, 'so much endeavor in this world; when I take you back to Godhead everything will be easy and sublime'; and when the Swami complained sankirtan was difficult, Prabhupada replied, 'When did I ever say that preaching is easy? Just you continue.'

The Paris charanamrita story illustrates the three sources of great mercy from the spiritual master, the remnants of his fruit/food, the dust of his feet, and the water that washed his feet, obtained through a grueling three-month Metro book-distribution marathon.
references: Chaitanya-caritamrita, Madhya-lila 19.151 — 'brahmanda bhramite kona bhagyavan jiva, guru-krsna-prasade paya bhakti-lata-bija' (quoted as 'brahmanda brahmatikonya... guru krishna prashad... bhakti ladbhij'); quoted to the airline agent to explain that the soul wanders through the universes since time immemorial and receives the seed of the devotional creeper only by the mercy of guru and Krishna.

Bhagavad-gita 4.34 — 'tad viddhi pranipatena pariprasnena sevaya' (quoted as 'tad vidi paripatena'); cited to argue that every intelligent man and woman should approach and accept a bona fide spiritual master.

Bhagavad-gita 2.13 — 'dehino 'smin yatha dehe kaumaram yauvanam jara' (quoted as 'dehino sminyutare... hovanam yovanam jada'); quoted on the plane about the embodied soul passing through boyhood, youth, and old age (and from body to body).

Bhagavad-gita 18.66 — 'sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam saranam vraja' (quoted as 'sarva dharmam padi... mam ekam... saranam'); the verse he read from his Bhagavad-gita on the plane instead of watching the in-flight movie.

Bhagavad-gita — paraphrased as 'Krishna says I am adventure'; cited (exact verse not clearly identifiable) to describe how spreading Krishna consciousness, not material pioneering, is the real adventure.

Srimad Bhagavatam 1.1.1 — 'janmady asya yatah'; the first verse of the Bhagavatam, referenced as the verse Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakura lectured on for three months in Dhaka; the Bhagavatam is also cited as the essence and scriptural basis of Krishna consciousness.
'Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya' — the Vasudeva (dvadasakshara) mantra from Srimad Bhagavatam; recited by the speaker to open his very first Bhagavatam class, seventy-two hours after joining.

Chaitanya-caritamrita — the pastime of Mukunda Datta, whom Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu declared He would accept only after a million births, and who danced in ecstasy that acceptance was at least guaranteed; cited as an example of a Vaishnava's faith in the spiritual master's word.

Chaitanya-caritamrita, Madhya-lila (Kshira-chora Gopinatha of Remuna) — the pastime of Madhavendra Puri and the cup of sweet rice (kshira) hidden and delivered by the Gopinatha deity/pujari, which he relished and preserved; cited in parallel to the speaker keeping Prabhupada's orange-peel maha-prasada for six months.

Commentaries of Vishvanatha Chakravarti Thakura (in Sanskrit and Bengali) — named as among the reference books in Prabhupada's heavy suitcase that Prabhupada used for his translation and purport work.
